card.name: Words just before a fold-change amount
card.fires_on: The word or gap right after a verb or phrase of increase (increased, nearly, greater than, less than) and just before a multiplier such as 2-fold or threefold. Seen mostly in drug-interaction and risk statements.

modes.label: Increase verb before fold
modes.description: The word "increased" after a drug level, AUC or half-life, right before a fold amount.
modes.example: triazolam half-life and AUC<< increased>> 4 fold and peak concentrations increased

modes.label: Comparison words before a number
modes.description: Words like "than", "nearly" or an empty gap between a comparison and a number with -fold or percent.
modes.example: who use NSAIDs had a greater<< than>> 10-fold increased risk for developing

card.writes: It lowers words meaning "indicate" and slightly favors other words, which fits a number expected next rather than an "indicated" phrase.
card.plain: It fires on the spot just before a statement of how many times higher a drug level or risk went.
